completion_verification.method: unique record identities and per-batch detector counts versus saved input manifest

multiplicity.primary: Benjamini-Hochberg across all 88 prespecified detector × batch × metric slots
multiplicity.unavailable_slots: No p-value is fabricated; unavailable tests contribute p=1 placeholders only to the adjustment denominator
multiplicity.sensitivity: Holm familywise adjustment across the same 88 slots; valid under arbitrary test dependence when individual p-values are valid
multiplicity.evidence_rule: Complete expected image accounting, global BH q < 0.05 and field-bootstrap 95% mean-difference interval excludes zero
multiplicity.partial_results: Provisional only; completing the run changes available fields, tests and estimates. No early-stopping inference is claimed.

sampling.reference_split: reference_holdout only; every train field and development-reviewed field excluded

equivalence.reason: No prespecified physically justified equivalence margins or material tolerances

development_reference_exclusion.reason: The post-classifier appearance-support gate was selected using the pilot view of Batch 3 field 0grcilhi. Its detector views are development data, not untouched reference inference data.

limitations: Differences refer to supported 2D appearance masks, not verified chemical phases or manufacturing defects.
Detector views of the same field are paired observations. They are never pooled as independent specimens or counted as independent confirmations.
One batch per condition provides no independent batch replication. Dependence between sampled fields can invalidate bootstrap and permutation uncertainty; specimen identities are unavailable.
BH relies on dependence assumptions; Holm is also reported because metrics and detector views are correlated. Neither adjustment repairs invalid field exchangeability.
Failure to detect a difference is inconclusive about equivalence or acceptable material; no equivalence test is possible without justified margins.
Unresolved pixels can fragment components and hide interfaces. Differences in unknown coverage can change every geometry measurement.
Interface density and image-y slopes retain native pixel units. Physical pixel size and image-y specimen orientation are unverified; changes in magnification or preparation can affect comparisons.
Largest-component fraction describes an observed 2D mask, not 3D transport connectivity. No Bruggeman departure is inferred.
